basedOn.note: every v6 expectation kept verbatim (id, severity, owner, check, args, text, predicted). New: s3b.on-topic, s3b.not-off-topic, s3b.answer-kept; s4.elapsed-true, s4n.elapsed-true; step s4c-change-nudge; step s12-stop-nudge; s9.change-not-repeated.

world.note: developer flags of the all-on world only; the product defaults stay off. budgets "bridge": the bridge's turn_context budgets (warm 800 / cold 1,500 ms). v6: EGDESK_INRUN_MESSAGES=on (L2 c17) so a message typed while the run works is taken into the run and handed to the session heartbeat. v7: wording "faithful": a checked draft is revised the way the revision prompt asks (keep the sentences that were not listed, restate the listed ones), so what the person sees in s3b is judged on the product chain and not on a fixed sentence.

action-relevance.note: L7's action-relevance rule, one developer flag for both sides (product default off): the context selection (L7 c20) and turn memory (L7 c21, 9186fd5, ACTION_MEMORY_RULE; in int/c14). Main turns the switch on for a run.

how: Judged only from the results file of a run: what the person sees after each step and the Decision requests of that step. Hard = the journey is broken for the person if it fails; soft = expected but known to be fragile or already reported. "predicted" records what this lane expects to fail and why, written before the real run. v2 adds expectations for what the first real run (c16) showed was wrong or misleading for the person although no v1 expectation covered it. v3 adds a genuine recall step and person-level checks of what changed since c16. The scripted subjective model now follows what the product hands it: the recording rule (no promise to record), the choices a task note lists, and the waited-on fact of a note prompt. v4 turns on L7's two turn-memory flags in the world, counts page bodies rather than page headers, and adds the owner question. v5 adds switches: developer flags a run turns on by name, recorded in the results, with expectations judged only under them. v6 adds an in-run nudge: while the long command runs the person asks why it stopped; one true progress reply is expected, no repeated wait message, and the command is not interrupted. v7 adds the other two in-run messages: a change ("그거 말고 B부터 해줘", five seconds after the status nudge, same command) and a stop ("그만해, 그거 하지 마", ten seconds into a second long command at the end of the journey). The Decision side (does the model read the change as a change, the stop as a stop) is measured on the real answers; the engine side is judged by code on what reached the scripted engine (steer, interrupt) and what the person sees. It also adds a check that the seconds a writer prompt gives for the work match the run's real age, and that the answer the person sees in s3b is about what they asked.
caps: Per step: about three times the requests and two and a half times the estimated input tokens of the dry run (independentEstimate of helper/egdesk-decision-real-runner.mjs), at least 4 requests and 4000 tokens. The journey total is capped separately (default 80000 tokens, 80 requests). The recall step s3b uses the same rule. The owner-question step s8b uses the same rule.
